DeVonta Smith draws a plus matchup — JAX concede 68 yds/game to WR1s (league ~58), and PHI funnel 25% of targets his way. A rec-yards spot.

The JAX welcome the PHI as underdogs of 2.5, with the total set at 43.5 — a market that implies a PHI 23–20 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 26% of its snaps with PHI in front, 39% within one score, and 34% with PHI chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

This is a coin-flip script. With only 2.5 points separating them, neither team projects to spend much time in a blowout state — most of the game lives in the 'close' bucket, where play-calling stays balanced and usage tracks each player's established role rather than being distorted by score. In tight games the stars on both sides see their normal, dependable workloads, and there is less garbage-time leakage to backups.

The Key Matchups

Tough sledding for Saquon Barkley — JAX are stingy against the run (109 yds/game, well below the ~120 norm); lean under on his rushing line.

Tough sledding for Chris Rodriguez Jr. — PHI are stingy against the run (112 yds/game, well below the ~120 norm); lean under on his rushing line.

Jalen Hurts has a passing-yards tailwind — JAX allow 252 pass yds/game (vs ~230).

Sneaky value on Dontayvion Wicks (WR2) — JAX leak 44 yds/game to the WR2 role, above the ~36 norm.

Sneaky value on Parker Washington (WR2) — PHI leak 42 yds/game to the WR2 role, above the ~36 norm.

Parker Washington faces a tough cover — PHI hold WR1s to just 52 yds/game (vs ~58); a rec-yards under lean.

Touchdown Board

Saquon Barkley is a bell-cow (77% of carries) meeting a defense that allows 0.49 RB rushing TDs/game — strong anytime-TD equity.

Dallas Goedert is a live anytime-TD dart — JAX are leaky to tight ends in the end zone (0.31 TE TDs/game vs ~0.24).

PHI pound it at the goal line (36% pass in the red zone) — Saquon Barkley owns the rushing-TD equity.

PHI — a run-heavy offense

PHI are one of the league's more run-committed offenses: on early downs while leading, they pass just 37% of the time, against a league average of 44% — a genuine clock-bleeding identity, not noise (it holds after shrinking their sample toward the league).

Saquon Barkley (15 carries, 70 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

DeVonta Smith projects for 6 targets and 54 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Dallas Goedert (TE, 6 targets, 51 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

JAX — a balanced offense

JAX are a balanced offense — their run/pass split by game state tracks the league closely (43% pass when leading vs 44% average), so their players' usage is driven more by role than by any strong situational lean.

Chris Rodriguez Jr. (10 carries, 49 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Parker Washington projects for 7 targets and 54 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Brenton Strange (TE, 5 targets, 36 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 2-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.

This preview and the projections below regenerate through the week as injuries, weather and line moves update the inputs.
